title: Address a Cook in their own grammatical form
objective: Convert every gendered string to an ICU select on the Cook's stored form, so Kafoo stops addressing half its Cooks in the wrong gender. ADR-0010.
acceptance_criteria: the Kitchen Profile conversation asks the fifth question, and the code says why a question that looks like a failure to infer is the right call here
all 86 gendered strings are ICU select in both ARB files, Arabic written first (the estimate of 56 predated E2 nearly doubling the file)
97 call sites in lib/ read the preference through AddressFormScope; the Customer-facing strings describing a Cook read the COOK's stored form, not the reader's
the localization parity check is extended to compare placeholders and select branches, not only key presence — the sweep must fix the check, not trust it
notes: The fifth question's wording is the founder's, approved 2026-08-05: عشان أكلمك صح — أقولّك "كمّل" ولا "كمّلي"؟ — built from first-person verbs only, because a question asked to learn the Cook's form cannot itself be gendered. EXCLUSIVE because it rewrites both ARB files and ~56 call sites across every feature. Every user-facing package touches the ARBs, so nothing else can run beside it without a merge nobody wants to resolve. It also changes verify.sh, which every other package depends on to know whether it passed. Not split further: converting the strings without the call sites leaves the app broken, and extending the parity check after the conversion means the conversion shipped unchecked.
completion_notes:
Landed in two pieces. T093 first, in PR #33: the parity check had to be able to see a broken translation before 86 strings were converted, because a conversion that ships past a check which cannot fail is worse than no check. T090/T091/T092 here.

Founder decision 2026-08-06 unblocked it: Customers are addressed as men for now, so the four Customer-facing strings keep their Customer-directed verbs ungendered and switch only the Cook-describing clause on cookForm. No new personal-data field for Customers. ADR-0010 records it as a deferral rather than a conclusion.

One deliberate departure from the brief: the preference reaches widgets through an InheritedWidget (AddressFormScope), not a Riverpod provider. The app has no ProviderScope above the Navigator — E1 shipped without a state-management package and E2 added Riverpod only inside the Meal feature — so a provider meant adding a root scope or converting every plain widget to a consumer. It is installed by MaterialApp.builder because a scope inside home is invisible to every pushed route.

PublicMealView takes a REQUIRED cookAddressForm. Nothing routes there yet, so there is no caller to get it right today; required is what stops E3's router inheriting a default filled in with the wrong person's grammar.

Mutation-tested: forcing icuAddressForm to masculine, making AddressFormScope.of ignore the tree, and dropping the answer from create() each turn test/address_form_test.dart red.
